assistant|companion_planting_tip: Plant companions around the perimeter of the cherry tomato bed as a trap crop
Plant companions at the same time as or slightly before cherry tomatoes

assistant|neem_oil_tip: Dilute neem oil 2-4 teaspoons per quart of water per product instructions
Spray all plant surfaces including leaves, stems, and soil
Target aphid hotspots: undersides of leaves, stem joints, flower buds
Avoid applying neem oil during peak sun hours; apply early morning or evening
Mixing neem oil with mild dish soap enhances effectiveness
Neem oil works slowly; be patient
assistant|aphid_control_method: Insecticidal soap: gentle non-toxic pesticide mixed with water
Horticultural oil: refined mineral oil that suffocates aphids
Ladybugs: natural aphid predators to introduce to the garden
Lacewings: generalist predators effective against aphids
Parasitic wasps (Aphidius ervi) prey on aphids
Fine-mesh screens over pepper plants to block aphids
Row covers to prevent aphids from flying onto plants
Remove weeds regularly to eliminate aphid habitat
Improve air circulation to reduce humidity and aphid spread
Water pepper plants at the base; avoid overwatering
Pyrethrin: natural pesticide from chrysanthemum flowers
Diatomaceous earth around plant base dehydrates and kills aphids
assistant|beneficial_insect_advice: Release ladybugs in large numbers (1,000-2,000) to control aphids

Select species specific to your region and pest
Release predators when aphid populations are present but not severe
Hoverfly larvae feed on aphids; attract with flowers
